item.text: The requirements exceed a theoretical stiffness bound: with the amm Ti6Al4V constants, a 22% solid fraction permits a bulk modulus of at most 9.94 GPa. That is below the requested 18.1 GPa, so no geometry in scope can meet both limits.

arguments.note: For the amm Ti6Al4V isotropic solid, E_s=113.8 GPa and nu_s=0.342, so K_s=120.042194 GPa and G_s=42.399404 GPa. The Hashin-Shtrikman solid/void upper bound on hydrostatic bulk stiffness, applicable to cubic cells, is K_eff <= f*K_s*(4*G_s/3)/((1-f)*K_s+4*G_s/3). It increases with solid fraction f; at f=0.22 it is 9.942259 GPa, below the required 18.1 GPa. Hence the requirements are infeasible for all stated families, independent of cell size. Meeting 18.1 GPa requires at least f=0.3567344 (35.67%) even under this theoretical bound; that necessary condition does not guarantee an achievable design. LPBF manufacturability is outside the model.
